objective_for_doctor: A 62-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have sharp pain, painful mouth ulcers or sores, and chronic fatigue.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having sharp pain and painful mouth ulcers or sores, and I also feel really tired all the time. I’m also short of breath, and I’ve noticed red skin lesions on my body, plus I’m here because I was told I have high blood pressure.
Dr. Agent: I’m Dr. Agent—thanks for sharing. When did your mouth ulcers start, how often do they recur, and do you have fever or weight loss?
The mouth ulcers started pretty recently—within the last few days, I think. They’re painful and keep coming back when I get them, but I can’t say an exact schedule. I don’t have fever or weight loss.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few quick questions—any similar sores on your genitals or eyes, and are you having trouble swallowing or bleeding gums? Also, tell me about the shortness of breath: does it happen at rest or only with exertion?

No, I don’t have sores on my genitals or in my eyes. I’m not having trouble swallowing and I’m not bleeding gums. For the shortness of breath, it feels significant and it’s not only with exertion—I can get it even when I’m resting.

Doctor: Thank you. Do the red skin lesions look like flat spots or raised bumps, and are they tender or itchy—also, have you noticed any new medications (especially antibiotics, anti-seizure meds, NSAIDs) or recent infections in the last month?

They look like red lesions that are there on my skin. They’re not really itchy, and I’d say they’re more painful than tender. I haven’t started any new medications recently, and I don’t think I had a new infection in the last month.

Doctor: I’ll examine you now—any rapid heart rate, oxygen levels low, or mouth lesions that look like a pattern; also, have you had painful swallowing, chest pain, or any leg swelling.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential, CMP, ESR_CRP  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: HIV_screening, HSV_oracle? (swab if possible), and chest X-ray.

I don’t have chest pain, painful swallowing, or leg swelling. I’m not sure about my heart rate or oxygen levels, and I don’t know how the mouth lesions look “in a pattern” from the outside—I just know they’re very painful.

Dr. Agent: I’m going to look closely in your mouth and skin and I need to check your vitals—please tell me: do you have any trouble breathing right now, and are the skin lesions blister-like, like target/bull’s-eye spots, or just red patches?  
Dr. Agent: Also, have you had any recent sores or rash on your hands/feet, and any new numbness or weakness?

Right now I’m still having trouble breathing. The skin lesions are just red patches/lesions—more red than blister-like or “bull’s-eye.” I haven’t noticed new sores or rash on my hands or feet, and I don’t have any new numbness or weakness.

Doctor: I’m going to ask two more focused questions: have the mouth ulcers involved your lips/gums/tongue (and can you see white/yellow centers), and do you have any recent/taking medications like allopurinol or antibiotics—even if started weeks ago?  
Doctor: Also, are you immunocompromised (HIV risk, steroids, chemotherapy), and have you noticed any eye pain/redness or burning when you urinate?

The mouth ulcers are on my mouth—lips and gums/tongue area, and I think there might be some white or yellow in the center, but I’m not 100% sure. I’m not taking any new meds like allopurinol or antibiotics. I don’t know of any immune problems, and I don’t have eye pain/redness or burning when I urinate.

Doctor: I’m going to proceed as if this is a systemic inflammatory or immune-driven process—can you tell me if the mouth sores started after any vaccination, new viral illness, or extreme stress, and whether the skin lesions began at the same time or later?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Viral_panel (HSV/PCR if available), urinalysis  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Dermatology_biopsy_of_skin_lesion (if accessible)

I don’t remember it starting right after a vaccination or a new viral illness, and I can’t tell you about extreme stress—nothing obvious. The skin lesions seemed to start around the same time as the mouth sores, maybe a little after but not long after.

Doctor: This cluster—acute painful oral ulcers with white/yellow centers plus new painful red skin lesions, along with significant shortness of breath—raises concern for a systemic immune/drug-free mucocutaneous disorder (not classic genital/eye HSV). I want urgent objective assessment now: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry_with_vitals, repeat_CBC_with_diff, CRP_ESR, and REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-ray (or CT if x-ray unclear).  

Doctor: Also, I need 1 more key history: have you been taking any over-the-counter meds/supplements in the last 1–2 months (including NSAIDs like ibuprofen, antibiotics from dental work, or herbal products)?
I’m having shortness of breath right now. I haven’t taken any new over-the-counter meds or supplements in the last 1–2 months—no ibuprofen or herbal products, and no antibiotics from dental work.

Doctor: Your combination of new painful mouth ulcers with white/yellow centers, painful red skin lesions, and *current* shortness of breath is concerning for a serious mucocutaneous/systemic inflammatory reaction (including severe drug-independent causes), so I want to confirm lung involvement urgently—REQUEST TEST: Urgent_vitals_with_pulse_ox, repeat_CBC_with_diff, CMP, CRP_ESR, and REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-ray (or CT if needed).  
Doctor: While those results are coming, I need one last key question: are you able to swallow liquids today, and do you have any rash/pain involving your eyes (burning/redness) or genital area?
I can swallow liquids today, yes. I don’t have any rash or pain involving my eyes, and I don’t have any genital sores or rash.

Doctor: Given painful oral ulcers with possible white/yellow centers plus new painful red skin lesions that started together, and *now* significant shortness of breath even at rest, I’m treating this as urgent mucocutaneous systemic disease rather than simple aphthous ulcers. REQUEST TEST: Immediate_ER_evaluation with repeat pulse oximetry, arterial blood gas if hypoxic, and Dermatology/Rheumatology consult; also request wound/skin/ulcer swab for HSV/VZV and consider serum autoantibodies (ANA, ENA) and direct immunofluorescence if biopsy is done.

Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Possible Stevens-Johnson syndrome / severe mucocutaneous reaction (SJS/TEN) or related autoimmune mucocutaneous eruption (e.g., Behçet-spectrum) — needs emergency confirmation and treatment due to current dyspnea.
